# Viraj Domadia

> Frontend-heavy full-stack developer in Bengaluru, India. Open to full-time and freelance work, on-site in Bengaluru or remote.

## About

Viraj Domadia is a frontend-heavy full-stack developer based in Bengaluru, originally from Mumbai. He works with React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, FastAPI, PostgreSQL and MongoDB. He builds the client, the server and the data layer as one product, and has four full-stack products live, from Tripsmith to Platter. He is completing an online MCA at Amity University (2025–2027) and is open to full-time and freelance work, on-site in Bengaluru or remote.

## Experience

Built Personal Invites end to end — create and share a digital invitation in under 30 seconds — including its FastAPI + PostgreSQL backend.
- IT Executive · Venus Vacations Pvt. Ltd (2024-07 → 2025-11): Ran the company’s IT and hardware. Alongside that, built the company website with a custom booking engine end to end — React front, Node/Express API, MongoDB — taken through internal review, not deployed.
- Application Development Associate · Accenture (2022-12 → 2023-07): Backup and support engineer on an enterprise client account: monitored NetBackup jobs, handled incidents and restores, and worked to SLAs in a large operations team.

## Tripsmith — case study

A travel agency’s booking site: an AI trip planner on the real catalogue, live seats, Razorpay checkout, GST invoices and an owner desk. Page: https://virajdomadia.com/projects/tripsmith

**The problem.** A small Indian tour agency sells fixed-date group trips: a set itinerary, a price per person and a limited number of seats per departure. Most run on WhatsApp, phone calls and a spreadsheet, so two people can pay for the same last seat, prices are worked out by hand, and nobody can see who changed a booking. Tripsmith is that agency’s own site, built so every seat, rupee and change is accounted for.

**What I built.** A Next.js site with 14 packages and 51 departures; package and destination pages are generated ahead of time and refresh on demand when the owner edits them. A FastAPI + Postgres API behind it. Customers book with live seats, add-ons, deals, early-bird prices and coupons; pay in full or a 25% deposit through Razorpay in test mode; get a PDF voucher and GST invoice; and sign in with an emailed 6-digit code to manage their trips. Customers can also join a waitlist on a sold-out date, change their date, save and compare trips, fill in traveller details and open a trip pack a week before they leave. The owner runs bookings, refunds, enquiries, packages, coupons, reviews and counter bookings over Razorpay Payment Links from an admin desk on the same API, with a departure calendar and reports that reconcile with the bookings CSV. On every public page an AI trip planner plans the trip in a chat: it searches live packages, checks dates and seats, opens the booking sheet pre-filled or hands the chat to a person, and the owner reads every conversation in a log.

**Key decisions.**
1. The server owns the price — Every quote is built on the server in whole paise: deal, then early-bird, then coupon, with add-ons added last. The browser never sends a price; the owner’s counter screen sends the total it expects and gets 409 price_changed if it moved.
2. Seats are held, not hoped for — Pressing Pay creates a 10-minute hold. The server locks the customer’s email or phone, then the departure row (FOR UPDATE). A test fires two orders for the last seat at once: exactly one wins, the other gets 409 sold_out.
3. All payments go through one capture function — The Checkout callback, the sync when Checkout closes, the webhook and payment links all lead into it. Signatures are checked with HMAC and a unique Razorpay payment id turns replays into no-ops. A payment that lands after the seats are gone is cancelled and refunded automatically through the Razorpay refund API.
4. History can’t be rewritten — Every booking change is written to booking_events, and a Postgres trigger refuses any UPDATE or DELETE on it. The owner sees it as a timeline, the customer as “Activity”.
5. The trip planner can only quote the database — A tool-calling agent on Gemini’s free tier, with our own loop instead of a framework. Every card and price comes from a tool result, and a guardrail checks the reply while it streams: an invented package or ₹ amount is replaced before it reaches the browser. Phone numbers and emails are removed before the model sees them, the site-wide cap lives in Postgres so it holds if the rate limiter fails, and when the free turns run out a no-AI finder takes over. 23 scripted real-model conversations pass, prompt injections included.

**Versions.**
- v1 Agency website (shipped): Catalog, search, package pages, enquiries + WhatsApp, itinerary PDF, owner admin.
- v2 Booking engine (shipped): Razorpay checkout, webhooks, accounts, deals, coupons, reviews, owner bookings desk.
- v2.5 Strengthen (shipped): Deposits, add-ons, early-bird, a waitlist, date change, refunds + GST documents, traveller details, a trip pack, saved trips + compare, counter booking, a departure calendar, reports and automatic emails.
- v2.6 Hardening (shipped): A four-track audit closed: money edge cases, demo-owner limits, CI gates, indexes, and every business rule served from one API.
- v3 AI trip planner (shipped): Chat that searches the catalog, checks live seats, opens the booking or hands off to a person; streaming guardrail, owner log, no-AI quick finder.

**Outcome.** Complete and live at tripsmith.virajdomadia.com, taking bookings in Razorpay test mode, with the AI trip planner on every public page at ₹0 a chat. Over 1,150 API tests and over 740 web tests, with a forced-race test on every lock path, plus 23 real-model evals run by hand (23/23). CI runs three jobs: web, api, and an OpenAPI contract check that fails if the generated types drift. The booking page scores 88 on PageSpeed mobile with the booking sheet open.
